publicationMetadataPlan.creator: OpenAI built-in image generation
publicationMetadataPlan.mediaDescription: Review-only scientific algorithmic anatomical or pathology reconstruction, not a photograph, scan, histology slide, patient record, or diagnostic image
publicationMetadataPlan.sourceUse: NLM MeSH supplies controlled condition identity and scope; official NIH sources supply conservative anatomical and communication boundaries only. No source image or design is copied.

reviewStandard: Current controlled condition identity, anatomically conservative and non-diagnostic representation, non-stigmatizing communication, complete pale edge field, crop-safe geometry, and exact prompt must be frozen before exactly one generation call per cleared route. Observed output controls later metadata.
promotionRule: No output may receive a registry key, public master, derivative, endpoint, schema node, or sitemap entry before immutable native-resolution review and exact-hash Control Tower acceptance.

assets.representationBoundary: Complete neutral reproductive anatomy plus ovarian-cycle orientation; no blockage, lesion, ovarian-reserve claim, asserted cause, treatment, prognosis, or diagnosis.
Neutral intact brain, upper spinal cord, distributed sensory network, and muscle orientation; no tender-point map, lesion, damaged tissue, universal mechanism, severity, or diagnosis.
Stomach orientation plus a separate localized gland-forming mucosal focus; no gross specimen, diagnostic histology, subtype, invasion depth, spread, stage, prognosis, or diagnosis.
Broad stomach orientation plus one nonspecific localized mucosal growth; no glandular architecture, histologic or molecular subtype, invasion, spread, stage, prognosis, or diagnosis.
One representative non-perforated, non-bleeding gastric mucosal crater; no asserted Helicobacter, NSAID, or other cause, complication, severity, or diagnosis.
Complete upper-digestive and junction anatomy with short contained retrograde luminal flow; no universal sphincter defect, mucosal injury, complication, severity, or diagnosis.
